Procedure: Attended, full-night diagnostic polysomnography.
Clinical Indication: Excessive daytime sleepiness, reported snoring, and witnessed apneas.

Frequent respiratory events were noted throughout the night. The overall Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) was 42 events per hour, which is in the severe range. Impression: The findings are consistent with severe obstructive sleep apnea (OSA).
A follow-up appointment is recommended to discuss treatment options, including positive airway pressure (PAP) therapy. A subsequent PAP titration study under polysomnography is indicated to determine the optimal pressure for treatment.

You have now completed your colonoscopy procedure, which was performed with the aid of intravenous sedation. The sedative medications are very effective but have lingering effects that will impair your judgment, motor skills, and memory for up to 24 hours. For your personal safety and well-being, it is imperative that you (and your designated escort) carefully review and follow these detailed post-procedure instructions.
IMMEDIATE POST-PROCEDURE SAFETY (Next 24 Hours)
These restrictions are not recommendations; they are mandatory for your safety.
Transportation and Escort: You must be driven home by a responsible adult. You are strictly forbidden from driving a vehicle, operating a bicycle, or taking public transportation (bus, taxi, rideshare) alone.
Constant Supervision: A responsible adult must remain with you for the remainder of the day and overnight. The effects of anesthesia can increase the risk of falls, confusion, and accidental injury. This person's role is to assist you and to seek medical help should any complications arise.
Restricted Activities: You must avoid all of the following activities for a full 24 hours:
Operating any machinery, including power tools, kitchen appliances, and lawn equipment.
Impressions:
Negative Colonoscopy: Successful and complete colonoscopy to the terminal ileum. The quality of the bowel preparation was excellent, allowing for full mucosal visualization. There were no polyps, masses, inflammatory changes, or other abnormalities noted throughout the colon.
Procedure Findings: Your colonoscopy was entirely normal. No tissue samples (biopsies) were taken, so there will be no follow-up pathology report.
Follow-Up Schedule: Based on these normal findings and national guidelines, we recommend you repeat a screening colonoscopy in 10 years.

Fibrinogen: Negative. Albumin: Negative. Electron Microscopy Description: Electron microscopy confirms diffuse subendothelial and mesangial electron-dense deposits. Tuboreticular inclusions are present within endothelial cells. There is approximately 50% podocyte foot process effacementent. Skin, left arm: Malignant Melanoma; Nodular Type.

Microscopic Description:
The excision shows a nodular proliferation of atypical melanocyte extending from the epidermis into the deep dermis. The melanocytes are large, with irregular nuclear contours, prominent eosinophilic, nuclear, and abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm. Numerous mitotic figures, including atypical forms, are identified. The Breslow thickness is measured at 2.5 nm. Ulceration is present. There is no evidence of lymphovascular or perineural invasion.

Gene Description:
Received in formula: labeled with the patient's name and "left arm shave biopsy," is a single, circular piece of skin measuring 1.0 cm in diameter and 0.4 cm in thickness. The epidermis is focally ulcerated and contains a darkly pigmented, raised lesion measuring 0.7 cm in diameter.

Comments:
The features are those of a nodular malignant melanoma. The deep and peripheral margins are involved by invasal melanoma. Wide local excision with sentinel lymph node biopsy is recommended based on the Breslow depth and presence of ulceration. Clinical correlation is essential.

Biomarkers:

Result: Positive
Interpretation: A BRAF V600E mutation was detected in the tumor cells. This finding has therapeutic implications, as patients with BRAF-mutated melanoma may benefit from targeted therapy.

Prostate, left base: Adenocarcinoma, Gleason Score 4+3=7 (Grade Group 3)
Microscopic Description:
Sections show prostatic acini replaced by infiltrative, poorly-formed cribriform glands (Gleason pattern 4) and individual discrete glands (Gleason pattern 3). The malignant glands are lined by cells with enlarged nuclei, prominent nucleoli, and scant cytoplasm. Perineural invasion is identified. The tumor involves approximately 60% of the core tissue examined.
Gross Description:
Received in formalin labeled "prostate, left base" are four tan-white cylindrical tissue cores, ranging from 1.1 to 1.4 cm in length. All tissue submitted in one cassette.
Comments:
The findings are consistent with prostatic adenocarcinoma, Gleason Score 7. The presence of a dominant Gleason pattern 4 and perineural invasion are adverse prognostic factors. Correlation with serum PSA levels and clinical staging is recommended.
Biomarkers:
Immunohistochemical stains for high molecular weight cytokeratin (HMWCK) and p63 are negative in the malignant glands, supporting the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. No further molecular biomarker testing indicated on this specimen.

The patient was educated on her asthma action plan, the signs of a severe exacerbation requiring emergency care, and the importance of adherence to her controller medication. She will follow up with her primary care physician in 3-5 days.
